title: School and College Enrollment Validation
text:
This site checks the PopulationSim synthetic population behind WFRC’s travel demand model against real school and college enrollment. The study area is Box Elder, Davis, Weber, Salt Lake, and Utah counties. K-12 enrollment is compared by school district. College enrollment is compared by county.
PopulationSim does not control on school enrollment, so each comparison runs two ways:

Enrollment status (the real test). The synthetic population’s school-grade label (SCHG) is uncontrolled, so it is compared directly with actual enrollment.
Age population (a sanity bound). Age is controlled in PopulationSim. The population in the school-age band should meet or exceed enrollment. It is not expected to match exactly.

title: School and College Enrollment Validation
text:
Known limitations

Box Elder is only partly inside the model region. Synthetic persons exist only inside model MAZs, so Box Elder needs clipping to the model boundary before it can be compared. That clip is still a TODO.
USHE and IPEDS are not like-for-like. USHE covers public institutions only and is Academic Year

IPEDS includes private institutions and is fall 2023. The county validation has an option to include private institutions.

Residence against location. Synthetic college counts are where students live. IPEDS counts by institution location, and USHE counts by site.
Charter schools are included in the district totals. Whether Utah DOE credits their enrollment to the resident district has not been checked against DOE’s published totals.
Online-only schools have no geographic catchment, so they are left out of the district totals and reported separately.
Private schools (NCES Private School Universe Survey) appear on the enrollment page but not in the district validation table.

Code, setup, and how to re-render the site are in the project README.

title: Synthetic Population
text:
This script produces the “synthetic” half of the validation schema: PopulationSim’s estimate of how many K-12 students and college students live in each district and county, to compare against the real enrollment numbers from 2_enrollment.qmd.

Objective: count synthetic persons by school district and by county, to compare with DOE and NCES. By district: sch_grade (every person with SCHG 1-14, at any age, matching DOE’s totalk12 + preschool and NCES’s K-12 + PK) and age_3_18 (every person aged 3-18, counted independently, a sanity bound since age is controlled in PopulationSim). By county: undergraduate (SCHG 15) and graduate (SCHG 16) at any age, and age_18_24 (population aged 18-24, a sanity bound).
What it reads: PopulationSim’s synthetic person output (local-only, under _data/raw/populationsim/ABM/1_Inputs/ScenarioBaseSample/1_PopulationSim/output/, gitignored). The dorm and group-quarters students are in the same file, so no second file is needed. It also reads the school and college crosswalks from 1_geography.qmd.
MAZ join: each person has a maz_id. The MAZ rows in crosswalk_school.csv give each person a school district, and the MAZ rows in crosswalk_college.csv give each person a county.
Known gaps: college counts are residence-based and include every enrolled resident, while IPEDS counts by institution location and USHE counts public institutions only. The two sides differ in definition, not only in data.
Box Elder: handled last. The MPO/TDM model region only partly covers the county, so its synthetic counts need to be clipped to the model boundary (1_geography.qmd’s model_boundary layer) before comparison. This is still a TODO.
Output: written to _data/intermediate/. synthetic_k12_by_district.csv has district persons (sch_grade, age_3_18). synthetic_college_by_county.csv has county persons (undergraduate, graduate, age_18_24). synthetic_by_district_level.csv and synthetic_age_by_district.csv hold the school-level and single-year-age breakdowns that the validation charts use.

title: Synthetic Population
text:
2. Classify students


Show code
# Same rules as PopulationSim's PersonType_Label (2_InputPreperation_Seed2.ipynb, person-type rules):
# SCHG 1-14 is pre-college and SCHG 15 or higher is college. K-12 is pre-college at ages 6-18;
# University student is college at age 16 or older.
# College at any age: SCHG 15 is undergraduate and SCHG 16 (beyond bachelor's) is graduate
persons["undergraduate"] = persons["sch_grade"].eq(15)
persons["graduate"] = persons["sch_grade"].eq(16)
persons["age_18_24"] = persons["age"].between(18, 24)
# Nursery/preschool (SCHG 1) through grade 12 (SCHG 14), at any age. Matches DOE's totalk12 + preschool
# and NCES's K-12 + PK. Age is counted separately below, so this flag has no age condition.
persons["grade_1_14"] = persons["sch_grade"].between(1, 14)
persons["age_3_18"] = persons["age"].between(3, 18)

title: Geography
Geography
text:
Overview
This script builds the geographic crosswalk that every later step in this project joins against.

Objective: tie every Census block in the Wasatch Front region (Box Elder, Davis, Weber, Salt Lake, and Utah counties) to the school district and county it falls in, and to the K-12 school(s) and college(s) located in it — so that PopulationSim’s synthetic population (3_synthetic.qmd) and real enrollment data (2_enrollment.qmd) can both be rolled up to district/county level as exact joins, with no area-weighting or estimation involved.
What it pulls: county, school district, Travel Analysis Zone (TAZ), and Census block boundaries; K-12 school and college locations from both UGRC/SGID (the state-preferred source) and NCES (kept alongside, not as a replacement, so schools and colleges can also be joined back to federal CCD/IPEDS data by ID); and the WFRC/MAG travel demand model boundary, used later to handle Box Elder County’s partial coverage in that model. TAZ boundaries come from WFRC’s WasatchFrontTAZ feature service rather than the TDM-GEO-AnalysisZones repo directly, so the pull stays current without tracking that repo’s releases — TAZID is what is kept as a reference layer. The synthetic join uses MAZ, not TAZ. MAZ boundaries come from a draft microzone layer supplied for Utah (_data/raw/geometry/microzones_draft_*.zip), not yet a published WFRC layer. Block boundaries are still cached and checked, but no crosswalk uses them.
Output: two crosswalks, one per use. _data/intermediate/crosswalk_school.csv maps each K-12 school (UGRC, NCES public, NCES private) and each MAZ to its district. _data/intermediate/crosswalk_college.csv maps each college (UGRC, NCES) and each MAZ to its county. MAZ rows appear in both files, so PopulationSim output rolls up through MAZ rather than through blocks. Section 10 checks coverage and maps the study area (Figure 1).

text:
3. Travel Analysis Zone (TAZ) boundaries


Show code
taz_boundary_path = paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "taz_boundary.gpkg"

# 1. Download only if not already cached locally
if not taz_boundary_path.exists():
    taz_url = (
        "https://services1.arcgis.com/taguadKoI1XFwivx/ArcGIS/rest/services/"
        "WasatchFrontTAZ/FeatureServer/0/query"
    )
    taz_pages = []
    offset = 0
    while True:
        page = gpd.read_file(
            f"{taz_url}?where=1=1&outFields=*&f=geojson"
            f"&orderByFields=FID&resultOffset={offset}&resultRecordCount=2000"
        )
        if page.empty:
            break
        taz_pages.append(page)
        offset += len(page)
        if len(page) < 2000:
            break
    all_taz = pd.concat(taz_pages, ignore_index=True).to_crs(constants["crs"])

    count_resp = requests.get(f"{taz_url}?where=1=1&returnCountOnly=true&f=json").json()
    assert len(all_taz) == count_resp["count"], (len(all_taz), count_resp["count"])

    all_taz["county_fips"] = all_taz["CO_FIPS"].astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(3)

    all_taz.to_file(taz_boundary_path)

title: Enrollment
Enrollment
text:
Overview
This script produces the “real enrollment” half of the validation schema — the numbers PopulationSim’s synthetic population (3_synthetic.qmd) gets compared against.

Objective: get district-level K-12 enrollment and county-level college enrollment from real, non-synthetic sources, joined through the school and college crosswalks built in 1_geography.qmd.
What it pulls: Utah DOE enrollment (public schools only, from UGRC’s own per-school counts), NCES enrollment by district (public via CCD); NCES private-school enrollment (Private School Universe Survey), reported in section 3 but not in the district validation table; USHE enrollment by institution and site (the WFRC data request, not a home-ZIP file, so its geography is the institution’s site); and IPEDS by county (fall 2023 campus-based enrollment, institutional control, and full-time/part-time detail).
Known gaps:

Charter schools are counted as public schools in the district totals. Whether Utah DOE credits their enrollment to the resident district has not been checked against DOE’s published totals.
NCES private-school enrollment is by school location, not residence.
USHE is Academic Year 2025 and covers public institutions only. IPEDS is fall 2023. Neither matches the ~2023 vintage used everywhere else, and no 2023-24 USHE extract is on file.

Output: CSVs in _data/intermediate/. The validation pages read the district and county totals (real_enrollment_by_district.csv, real_enrollment_by_county.csv) and the level breakdowns (real_by_district_level.csv, real_college_by_county_level.csv). university_modality_compare.csv feeds the section 8 chart. ipeds_fulltime_parttime.csv is written but not charted yet. _outputs/ is created here, but nothing is written to it.

# Public schools only
ugrc_public_schools = gpd.read_file(
    paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "ugrc_school.gpkg",
    sql="""
        SELECT * FROM ugrc_school
        WHERE privateschool = 'False'
          AND onlineschool IS NOT 'Y'
    """,
)

# Join school -> district via the school crosswalk (point-in-polygon, one row per school) rather than
# matching the school's own `leaname` text against the district boundary's `name` text.
doe_crosswalk = school_crosswalk[
    (school_crosswalk["Unit"] == "school") & (school_crosswalk["Source"] == "UGRC")
]
assert (doe_crosswalk.groupby("ID")["District Name"].nunique() <= 1).all(), (
    "UGRC school ID maps to two districts"
)
doe_crosswalk = doe_crosswalk.drop_duplicates(subset=["ID"])

# The UGRC layer repeats some school IDs. Exact copies (Minersville, 201, is listed twice with the same
# count) are dropped so they are not double-counted. Separate records that share an ID (Grouse Creek,
# 218, an elementary and a secondary with different counts) are both kept and summed.
doe_grade_cols = ["preschool", "k"] + [f"grade{i}" for i in range(1, 13)]
ugrc_unique = (
    ugrc_public_schools[["schoolid", "schoolname", "totalk12", *doe_grade_cols]]
    .drop_duplicates()
    .assign(doe_students=lambda df: df["totalk12"] + df["preschool"].fillna(0))
)

# Left join, so schools with no crosswalk match are kept visible instead of silently dropped
doe_schools = (
    ugrc_unique.assign(schoolid=lambda df: df["schoolid"].astype("Int64").astype(str))
    .merge(doe_crosswalk[["ID", "District Name"]], how="left", left_on="schoolid", right_on="ID")
)
assert len(doe_schools) == len(ugrc_unique), "school join changed the row count"

unmatched_doe_schools = doe_schools[doe_schools["District Name"].isna()]
print(
    f"DOE schools with no district match: {len(unmatched_doe_schools)} "
    f"({unmatched_doe_schools['doe_students'].sum():,.0f} students, excluded from district totals)"
)

# groupby drops the unmatched rows (NaN district), so they are excluded from the totals below
doe_enrollment_by_district = (
    doe_schools.groupby("District Name")["doe_students"]
    .sum()
    .rename("doe_enrollment")
    .reset_index()
)

Show code
# Matches constants["data_year"] -- the vintage pulled in 1_geography.qmd
nces_public_school = gpd.read_file(paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "nces_public_school.gpkg")

nces_crosswalk = school_crosswalk[school_crosswalk["Source"] == "NCES public"]
assert (nces_crosswalk.groupby("ID")["District Name"].nunique() <= 1).all(), (
    "NCES public ID maps to two districts"
)
nces_crosswalk = nces_crosswalk.drop_duplicates(subset=["ID"])

# DOE totalk12 is K-12 only: it equals the sum of k and grades 1-12 on every public, non-online row, and
# it excludes preschool. NCES TOTAL includes PreK, plus other codes (UG, AE, G13), so NCES is summed
# over KG-G12 to match the DOE definition. NCES codes a grade the school doesn't offer as -2; those
# cells count as zero students.
nces_k12_grades = ["KG"] + [f"G{i:02d}" for i in range(1, 13)]
assert (nces_public_school[nces_k12_grades] >= -2).all().all(), "NCES K-12 grade has an unexpected code"
nces_public_school["K12"] = nces_public_school[nces_k12_grades].clip(lower=0).fillna(0).sum(axis=1)

# PK (preschool) uses the same -2 "not offered" rule as the grades, so negative codes count as zero
assert (nces_public_school["PK"] >= -2).all(), "NCES PK has an unexpected code"
nces_public_school["PK_students"] = nces_public_school["PK"].clip(lower=0).fillna(0)
nces_public_school["nces_students"] = nces_public_school["K12"] + nces_public_school["PK_students"]

nces_enrollment_by_district = (
    nces_public_school[["NCESSCH", "nces_students"]]
    .drop_duplicates()
    .assign(NCESSCH=lambda df: df["NCESSCH"].astype(str))
    .merge(
        nces_crosswalk[["ID", "District Name"]],
        left_on="NCESSCH",
        right_on="ID",
    )
    .groupby("District Name")["nces_students"]
    .sum()
    .rename("nces_enrollment")
    .reset_index()
)

    hd_frequencies = pd.read_excel(z.open(hd_dict_name), sheet_name="Frequencies")

assert control_labels.get(2) == "Private not-for-profit", "IPEDS CONTROL code 2 changed"

# Every institution in the study counties that IPEDS covers, using campus-based enrollment: in-person
# plus hybrid (EFDENON + EFDESOM). Exclusively online students (EFDEEXC) are left out, since they don't
# attend a campus in the county. EFDELEV 2 is undergraduate and 12 is graduate (the subtotals add up).
ipeds_levels = {2: "Undergraduate", 12: "Graduate"}
nces_college_locations = gpd.read_file(
    paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "nces_college.gpkg", ignore_geometry=True
)
in_study_counties = nces_college_locations["county_fips"].isin(
    ["003", "011", "035", "049", "057"]
)
college_county = (
    nces_college_locations.loc[in_study_counties, ["UNITID", "county_fips"]]
    .dropna(subset=["UNITID"])
    .assign(UNITID=lambda df: df["UNITID"].astype(int))
    .rename(columns={"county_fips": "COUNTYFP"})
)

campus = ipeds_dist[ipeds_dist["EFDELEV"].isin(ipeds_levels)].copy()
campus[["EFDENON", "EFDESOM"]] = campus[["EFDENON", "EFDESOM"]].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").fillna(0)
campus["Level"] = campus["EFDELEV"].map(ipeds_levels)
campus["campus_based"] = campus["EFDENON"] + campus["EFDESOM"]
campus = (
    campus[["UNITID", "Level", "campus_based"]]
    .merge(college_county, on="UNITID")
    .merge(college_control, on="UNITID", how="left")
    .assign(Control=lambda df: df["Control"].fillna("Not available"))

# Weber State's Davis campus is counted in Davis County, using its share of USHE headcount among

    (ushe_2025_fall["Institution"] == "Weber State University")
    & ushe_2025_fall["Site"].isin(["Main Campus", "WSU - Davis Center"])

wsu = campus["UNITID"].eq(230782)

campus = pd.concat([campus, wsu_davis], ignore_index=True)

    campus.groupby(["COUNTYFP", "Level", "Control"])["campus_based"]
    .sum()
    .round()
    .rename("nces_enrollment")
    .reset_index()
)

# IPEDS, fall 2023 (same definitions as section 5)
ipeds_long = (
    ipeds_dist[ipeds_dist["EFDELEV"] == 1]
    .loc[lambda df: df["UNITID"].isin(list(university_names))]
    .assign(
        Institution=lambda df: df["UNITID"].map(university_names),
        **{
            "In-person only": lambda df: df["EFDENON"].fillna(0),
            "Hybrid (some DE)": lambda df: df["EFDESOM"].fillna(0),
            "Online only": lambda df: df["EFDEEXC"].fillna(0),
        },
    )
    .melt(
        id_vars=["Institution"],
        value_vars=["In-person only", "Hybrid (some DE)", "Online only"],
        var_name="Segment",
        value_name="Students",
    )
    .assign(Source="IPEDS")
)

# USHE, Academic Year 2025 Term 2 (full- and part-time). The "taught online" rows are the hybrid
# portion; USHE has no online-only category.
ushe_long = (
    ushe_2025_fall[ushe_2025_fall["Institution"].isin(list(ushe_names))]
    .assign(
        Institution=lambda df: df["Institution"].map(ushe_names),
        Segment=lambda df: df["Site"].eq("This portion of the course is taught online").map(
            {True: "Hybrid (some DE)", False: "In-person only"}
        ),
    )
    .groupby(["Institution", "Segment"], as_index=False)["Headcount"]
    .sum()
    .rename(columns={"Headcount": "Students"})
    .assign(Source="USHE")
)

modality_compare = pd.concat([ipeds_long, ushe_long], ignore_index=True)[
    ["Institution", "Source", "Segment", "Students"]
]
